hero.lead: We flag price anomalies in public procurement by comparing every contract against thousands of similar historical ones. Search, filter and read the evidence behind each alert, across {count} countries and counting.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: No technical knowledge needed. All the reasoning stays visible.
how.s1Text: Search contracts by country, buyer or category, or go straight to the list of anomalies already found.
how.s2Text: Every contract is checked against the NLP model (BERT + XGBoost, Paraguay and Colombia) and against a robust statistical layer (median + MAD) that runs across all countries.
how.s3Text: Each alert shows the kind of deviation, the buyer, the category and the contract itself — never just an isolated score.

home.title: Public contracts
home.subtitle: {n} contracts — {countries}. Each country has its own source; the details are below.

sources.title: Data sources by country
sources.lead: Every country publishes its procurement differently, and that changes how the amounts should be read. Here is each one's source and currency, with live figures.

note.PY: Historical dataset in OCDS format. Amounts are shown in USD adjusted for inflation (CPI) to the model's reference year, not the nominal value on the contract date.
note.CO: Two sources: the official datos.gov.co API (SECOP II, with real dates) and a dataset already processed by a third party (with model predictions but no dates). No per-date exchange rate is verifiable, so amounts stay in Colombian pesos.
note.CR: Live data from the Observatorio de Compra Pública, updated daily. The official system itself publishes the amounts already converted to dollars.
note.DO: Live DGCP API. Amounts in Dominican pesos, with no verifiable conversion to dollars.
note.PE: OCDS API from the open contracting portal. Only the awarded amount is ingested, never the tender's reference value. It is the only source here that also publishes the winning supplier and the CUBSO classification.
note.SV: Live COMPRASAL API. The country has used the dollar since 2001, so amounts arrive in USD. The data comes as purchase line items, not whole contracts.
note.BR: Federal government open-data API. It requires querying one organisation at a time, in windows of up to 365 days. Amounts in reais.
note.UY: Native OCDS 1.1, published per year. Amounts come per awarded line item and in several currencies; the one with the largest total in each award is used.

team.title: Founders
team.lead: This is built by a team that combines product and technical capabilities.

anomalies.title: Detected anomalies
anomalies.subtitle: Two independent signals: deviation from the NLP model and statistical deviation against similar contracts. {n} contracts flagged.
anomalies.note: This is NOT an accusation of corruption. The NLP signal measures the distance from the price the model predicted. The statistical signal compares the amount against the median of similar contracts from the same buyer, category or country, using a robust method (median + MAD over the log of the amount). The deviation column shows how far the amount sits from that reference: "+120%" is more than double, "×14" is fourteen times. When a contract carries both signals, they are shown separately.
anomalies.sourceTitle: Opens {country}'s official source in a new tab

contract.nlpDeviation: Deviation from the model's predicted value
contract.statDeviation: Deviation from the median of comparable contracts
contract.bothSignals: Both signals flag this contract, and they are entirely independent of each other.
contract.nlpOnly: This score comes only from the NLP model. There is no second, statistical signal confirming it for this contract yet.
contract.statOnly: This score comes only from the statistical method (median + MAD, with no AI model involved): there is no NLP prediction for this contract.
contract.treatAsSignal: Treat it as a signal worth investigating, not as a conclusion.

tenders.title: Prepare your bid
tenders.lead: Pick a country and a category to see the median price and typical range of similar contracts already awarded. It is a reference for pricing a competitive bid, not a guarantee of winning one.
tenders.note: This is not a list of open tenders or a way to submit a bid: Contractor AI has no scraper connected to the official portals. What it does offer, from data already ingested, is the reference price and a verified link to each country's real portal.
tenders.noCategories: Not enough contracts ingested per category in this country yet.
tenders.benchmarkError: The reference price could not be calculated.
tenders.typicalRange: Typical range: {low} – {high} · based on {n} similar contracts already ingested.

analyze.title: Analyze a contract
analyze.lead: Upload the document in whatever format you have. We compare it against contracts already ingested from the country you pick, using the same statistical layer (median + MAD) as the rest of the app: the verdict is fully statistical, with no AI involved. The plain-language summary is an optional step at the end.

onboarding.toggleTitle: How do you analyze a contract?
onboarding.s1Desc: Upload a PDF (native or scanned) or paste a link to the contract's official publication.
onboarding.s1Tip1: Scanned PDFs go through automatic OCR
onboarding.s1Tip2: Public links to documents work too
onboarding.s1Tip3: If OCR struggles, the suggested data may not be exact
onboarding.s2Desc: The system reads the document and suggests a title, amount, category and buying institution.
onboarding.s2Tip1: Check that the amount was picked up correctly
onboarding.s2Tip2: If OCR was imperfect, correct it by hand
onboarding.s2Tip3: The currency is filled in from the country
onboarding.s3Desc: The contract is compared against similar ones from the same country and category, using pure statistics and no AI.
onboarding.s3Tip1: Uses median + MAD, robust against extreme values
onboarding.s3Tip2: Shows the typical price range for similar contracts
onboarding.s3Tip3: The verdict rests on data alone and stays visible
onboarding.s4Desc: Generates a plain-language summary of the contract.
onboarding.s4Tip1: Only available with an API key configured
onboarding.s4Tip2: Not part of the verdict: it is context
onboarding.s4Tip3: Useful to grasp quickly what the contract is about
onboarding.q1Title: What counts as a high deviation?
onboarding.q1Desc: A contract whose amount is more than double that of similar contracts in the same country and category.
onboarding.q1Example: Road repair: similar contracts cost $50k and this one paid $150k.
onboarding.q2Desc: The amount is somewhat high but not anomalous. Factors the data does not capture, such as urgency or specificity, may explain it.
onboarding.q2Example: A contract 15% to 25% above the typical range.
onboarding.q3Title: How do I read the reference range?
onboarding.q3Desc: The typical range covers the middle 50% of similar contracts. Outside it is unusual.
onboarding.q3Example: If the typical range is $50k–$100k and the contract is $200k, it is worth investigating.
onboarding.f1Text: No AI and no arbitrary criteria in the verdict.
onboarding.f2Text: Uses median + MAD, so extreme values do not distort it.
onboarding.f3Text: The reference range and the full deviation stay visible.
onboarding.f4Text: Compares by country, category and buyer.
onboarding.f5Text: It is a signal to investigate, not a legal verdict.

The verdict above is purely statistical (median + MAD over the log of the amount, the same formula used across the app) against contracts already ingested from the same country and currency: no AI model takes part in that calculation. The plain-language summary below is generated by an external model, is optional, and is never the source of the verdict.

citizen.title: Citizen input
citizen.lead: This is a space for anyone to add context about this contract: pointing out something that looks irregular, or supplying information that explains it. It is not a formal complaints channel and does not replace the competent authorities.
citizen.placeholder: What do you notice about this contract?
citizen.tooShort: Say a little more: at least 5 characters.
citizen.sendError: The report could not be sent. Try again.
citizen.thanks: Thank you — your input now appears in the list above.

fav.title: Supplier favouritism and concentration
fav.lead: Finds patterns of market concentration, price favouritism, geographic favouritism and awards clustered in time, which can point to coordination between buyers and suppliers.
fav.selectFilters: Pick the filters and press Update to see the analysis.
fav.error: The analysis could not be loaded.
fav.priceLead: Suppliers paid above the market average in the same year.
fav.geoLead: Top suppliers per country: how concentrated each market is.
fav.temporalLead: Suppliers with 3 or more contracts in the same month, which can indicate coordination.
fav.i1Text: A highly concentrated market: risk of monopoly or collusion.
fav.i2Text: The supplier is consistently paid above the average.
fav.i4Text: Five or more awards in a month point to a high risk of coordination.
fav.i5Text: The supplier is flagged often and is worth a closer look.

dashboard.title: Institutional dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Aggregate view of {n} contracts {scope}: volume, trend and the rate of anomalies flagged by the statistical layer (median + MAD on the log of the amount).
dashboard.bestTitle: Institutions with the strongest procurement record
dashboard.bestNote: Institutions with at least {min} ingested contracts and the lowest share of open statistical anomalies, best first. Not an integrity certificate: just a reading of the same data used across the app.
dashboard.bestEmpty: Not enough institutions with {min}+ contracts for this filter.

heatmap.title: Anomaly rate by country and year
heatmap.note: Each cell is the share of that country's contracts in that year with an open statistical anomaly; the legend maps colors to rates. Hatched cells have fewer than {min} contracts, so their rate is unreliable.
heatmap.empty: No dated contracts to show yet.
